C17 has a superficially similar statute-quotation-to-proclamation structure, and C25 concerns a national monument, but neither supplies distinctive language or operative structure adapted in the child.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the flag of the United States shall hereafter be displayed at Fort McHenry National Monument and Historic Shrine at all times during the day and night","parent_excerpt":"do hereby direct that the flag of the United States be displayed on all Government buildings on June 14, 1948","explanation":"C12 shares the flag-display formulation, but this is ordinary language dictated by the common subject; the duration, legal authority, purpose, and operative effect materially differ."},{"child_excerpt":"Whereas the joint resolution of Congress ... contains the following provisions","parent_excerpt":"Whereas section 3228(f) of the Internal Revenue Code provides in part as follows","explanation":"C17 likewise quotes governing statutory text before an operative proclamation, but that generic statutory-recital structure does not establish reusable drafting."},{"child_excerpt":"displayed at Fort McHenry National Monument and Historic Shrine","parent_excerpt":"added to and reserved as a part of the Fort Matanzas National Monument","explanation":"C25 shares a national-monument setting, but its land-reservation, boundary-description, warning, and administrative provisions are absent from the child."}]}
